newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt members approve land claims deal.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt members approve land claims deal.

text.p: Parliamentary members of Australia's Liberal-National coalition government overwhelmingly endorsed Prime Minister John Howard's native title plan on Tuesday, a coalition spokesman said.

The spokesman said 35 parliamentarians had spoken at a joint party meeting earlier on Tuesday on Howard's 10-point plan to end a land dispute between Aborigines and farmers and miners and most expressed their support.
"The outcome of that was that the party room overwhelmingly approved the 10-point plan," the spokesman told reporters.
He said Howard would release an exposure draft of the legislation, which would contain more detail, but declined to give a date.
The detailed legislation would also have to receive coalition approval before it was introduced for debate in parliament, he said.

The key element of Howard's plan is the confirmation of farmers' rights to land they have leased since European settlement began more than 200 years ago, while also guaranteeing Aborigines limited access for traditional purposes.
It also reduces Aboriginal rights to negotiate over development and other uses of land and exempts cities, towns and water catchments from Aboriginal claims.

But the plan received harsh criticism from some members of the National Party, the junior partner in the coalition, who called for blanket extinguishment of native title in response to demands from their rural-based constituents.
They said Howard's compromise deal did not provide farmers with the certainty they needed to successfully continue their businesses.
But Aboriginal groups have disputed this, saying Howard's plan effectively wipes out native title.

Native title laws were introduced by the former Labor government three years ago, but became an urgent political issue when the High Court decided last December that land leased to farmers for generations could be liable to Aboriginal claim.
